text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Romania's first barter bank will open in Constanta at the end of the week.
- The National Oil Company says $100 million from the centralised hard currency energy fund will help finance oil and gas imports until the end of the year.
- The founding members of the troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA call for a change in the current management.
- Romania needs 2.0 million tonnes more wheat to meet domestic consumption requirements and the solution are either to import or to resort to the state reserves.
- The number of companies listed on the over-the-counter market now stands at 529.
- The national railway company SNCFR plans to buy 20,000 tonnes of tracks through the Bucharest commodities exchange.
- The European Union's Phare programme will assist Romania in improving the content of information supplied to foreign investors.
- Losses in the oil refining sector over the past two years amount to $278 million.
